bull.b: DoorDash’s TTM free cash flow of about $2.8B and rapid FCF growth indicate durable operating cash conversion. Strong cash generation funds strategic investments (fulfillment, autonomy, global tech), reduces reliance on external financing, and provides a buffer versus short-term margin volatility.

Accelerating DashPass adoption that outpaced the prior two-year period signals higher retention and increased order frequency. Greater subscription penetration raises gross profit per MAU, smooths revenue streams, and improves lifetime unit economics, supporting more predictable margins over months.

Expanding merchant products and advertising to 150k+ merchants (≈40% YoY growth) diversifies revenue beyond delivery commissions. Recurring merchant spend and ad monetization elevate take rate, deepen merchant retention, and create higher-margin, less cyclical revenue over the medium term.

bear.b: Despite profitability inflection, operating and net margins remain modest for a scaled platform. Limited margin buffers increase sensitivity to rising Dasher costs, competitive pricing pressure, or slower revenue growth, constraining the company’s ability to fund large investments without compressing profits.

Large programs—global tech unification, autonomy, fulfillment expansion—are capital- and execution-intensive. Delays, integration issues, or cost overruns could postpone expected unit-economics gains, absorb cash flows, and dent profitability and growth over the next several quarters.

Grocery requires inventory accuracy and physical infrastructure; many grocers lack reliable feeds. Solving this needs DashMart-like fulfillment and capital investment, increasing operational complexity and cost, which may slow grocery margin improvement and scale versus management timing expectations.
